воспользоваться.gloss: to take advantage of, to use

meanings.en: to take advantage of, to use
meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'спользоваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take advantage of, to use', paired with 'пользоваться'.

examples.trans: He took advantage of the moment.

examples.text: Ты просто воспользовался моей минутной слабостью.
examples.trans: You simply took advantage of my momentary weakness.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('someone else's, foreign').

examples.text: Вы так и берёте чужое без спроса?
examples.trans: So you just take other people's things without asking?
That's someone else's bag.

examples.text: Вы так и берёте чужое без спроса, да?
examples.trans: So you just take other people's things without asking, yes?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'knife' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Cutting a living person with a knife!
There is a sharp knife on the table.

examples.text: Нина, ну как ты могла? Живого человека ножом резать!
examples.trans: Nina, how could you? Cutting a living person with a knife!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'so that, in order to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So that there are witnesses.
I'm calling to say thank you.
So that there are witnesses, Samson.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'бить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to kill', paired with 'убивать'.

examples.trans: Do you want to kill me?
I'll kill you! (said in anger)

examples.text: Ты смотришь на меня так, как будто убить хочешь.
examples.trans: You look at me as if you want to kill me.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'enemy' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: She is our number-one enemy.
He has many enemies.

examples.text: С ней вообще нельзя разговаривать. Это наш самый главный враг.
examples.trans: You mustn't talk to her at all. She is our number-one enemy.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('young').

examples.text: Молодой человек, как на тест-драйв записаться?
examples.trans: Young man, how do I sign up for a test drive?
They have a young family.

examples.text: Молодой человек, а как на тест-драйв записаться?
examples.trans: Young man, how do I sign up for a test drive?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'person; (pl) people' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is a good person.
There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: May I have a look?
Can you smoke here?
Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh yeah?
Yes, it's me.
Oh yeah? When?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
I'm doing my homework.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.trans: Listen, Samson.
Yes, I'm listening.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Lyolya will definitely come!

examples.text: Я точно не помню его адрес.
examples.trans: I don't remember his exact address.

examples.text: Точно, полиция была! А что с машиной?
examples.trans: That's right, the police were there! And what about the car?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'two', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: In two weeks.
Two houses.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('red-haired, ginger, rust-coloured').

examples.text: Марина, скажите, в кого ваш мальчик такой рыжий?
examples.trans: Marina, tell me, who does your boy get that red hair from?
A ginger cat lives with us.

examples.text: В рыжего певца! Они приезжали к нам на концерт.
examples.trans: From the red-haired singer! They came to our town for a concert.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'hair' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Волосы не должны попасть в еду.
examples.trans: Hair must not fall into the food.

examples.text: Волосы не должны попасть в еду!
examples.trans: Hair must not fall into the food!
If they find even one hair — you'll be fired immediately!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: International noun in '-ция' (from Latin '-tio'), feminine declension. Common feminine noun meaning 'protest action; share, stock' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The students organized a peaceful protest action.

examples.text: Марина, давай заканчивать эту опасную акцию.
examples.trans: Marina, let's end this dangerous protest.

examples.text: Костик, мы сегодня идём на акцию?
examples.trans: Kostik, are we going to the rally today?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('second').

examples.trans: This is my second term.
The second lesson is hard.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

получать.gloss: to receive, to get; to earn

meanings.en: to receive, to get; to earn
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to receive, to get; to earn', paired with 'получить'.

examples.trans: How much do you earn?
I get letters.

examples.text: А почему нет? Продавец получает больше, чем преподаватель.
examples.trans: Why not? A sales assistant earns more than a lecturer.

meanings.note: Privative prefix 'бес-' ('without, -less', before voiceless consonants) (stem 'платно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: If they're late, the pizza is free.
Children get in free.

examples.text: Если опоздают, пицца бесплатно. Может, закажем?
examples.trans: If they're late, the pizza is free. Maybe we should order?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forgive; (imperative) excuse me', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.trans: Excuse me, who are you?
Forgive me.
Please forgive me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нимать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понять'.

examples.trans: I understand.
I want to go to the sea, you know?

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: How was it in Hungary?
As you all know...
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

получиться.gloss: to turn out, to work out

meanings.en: to turn out, to work out
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to turn out, to work out', paired with 'получаться'.

examples.trans: It will all work out!
He'll make a good doctor.

examples.text: Классный из тебя мэр получится, Самсон.
examples.trans: You'll make a great mayor, Samson.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кренне').

examples.text: Я вам искренне сочувствую, но мне пора работать.
examples.trans: I sincerely feel for you, but it is time for me to work.

examples.text: Мы искренне благодарим вас за помощь.
examples.trans: We sincerely thank you for your help.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я вам искренне сочувствую.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I sincerely sympathize with you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ожалеть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to regret, be sorry', paired with 'посожалеть'.

examples.text: Я очень сожалею о своих словах.
examples.trans: I deeply regret my words.

examples.text: Я сильно ошиблась и очень сожалею об этом.
examples.trans: I was very mistaken and deeply regret it.

examples.text: Ты действительно сожалеешь о своих словах?
examples.trans: Do you really regret your words?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: I'm in the office now.
I'll be right there.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning '(emphasis) after all, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.
But you've still got some.
I told you: no.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'менить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to replace', paired with 'заменять'.

examples.trans: We demand that house arrest be replaced.
Who will replace me tomorrow?

examples.text: Мы требуем заменить домашний арест. Нужна подписка о невыезде.
examples.trans: We demand that house arrest be replaced. What's needed is a travel ban.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: This house.
I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will bring', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.text: А я вот вам чаю с сушками принёс.
examples.trans: I've brought you some tea and bread rings.

examples.text: А что это ты в квартиру принёс?
examples.trans: And what is that you brought into the flat?

examples.text: Видишь, Аркаша, он собаку принёс тебе.
examples.trans: See, Arkasha, he brought you a dog.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'more; still; yet', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You've still got some.
You'll be sorry!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'time, occasion' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Just once.
Say it once more.
What do you mean, once?

просить.gloss: to ask, to request, to beg

meanings.en: to ask, to request, to beg
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask, to request, to beg', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.
Samsonov, I asked you not to!

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'щение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'forgiveness' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I apologise.
He is asking me to forgive him.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for; behind', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Thank you for your trust!
Thanks for the present.
What for?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'they', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They are building a centre.
History will punish them.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to pay', paired with 'заплатить'.

examples.trans: We pay well.
Who is paying?

examples.text: А вашу работу вернуть можно. И мы хорошо платим.
examples.trans: But we can get your job back for you. And we pay well.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'алат'). Common masculine noun meaning 'salad' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a salad.

examples.text: Седьмой столик заказал салат с трюфелями.
examples.trans: Table seven ordered a salad with truffles.

examples.text: Гость пришёл специально ради этого салата.
examples.trans: The guest came especially for this salad.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.
Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'account, bill, score' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Or a bank account.
Bring the bill, please.

examples.text: Или счёт в банке. Потому что они все обманщики.
examples.trans: Or a bank account. Because they are all cheats.
